name: SBA Communications
description: SBA is a tower REIT that leases antenna space on wireless towers to carriers. About two-thirds of revenue is U.S. site leasing (17,394 owned U.S. sites; T-Mobile 31.1%, AT&T 20.3% and Verizon 15.1% of total revenue), a quarter is site leasing in South and Central America and Africa, and 9% is site development (construction and permitting services for carriers). Leases run five to ten years with annual rent escalators, so earnings are mostly contracted; site leasing produces 97.9% of segment operating profit. In 2025 it bought over 7,000 sites from Millicom in Latin America, and it is buying back stock under a $1.5B plan.

gics.note: Conventional GICS sector and sub-industry as listed in Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies), read 2026-10-01; industry group and industry are not shown there. SEC SIC 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts).

employees.note: 663 based outside the U.S. and its territories

businessLines.name: Domestic site leasing
businessLines.how: Recurring rent from carriers under 5 to 10 year tenant leases with escalators and renewals; each added carrier adds nearly all-profit revenue.
businessLines.description: Antenna space on 17,394 owned U.S. and territory sites (72.6% of total site leasing revenue).

businessLines.name: International site leasing
businessLines.how: Recurring carrier rent in local currency or USD, escalators tied to inflation indices in some markets; more currency exposure.
businessLines.description: Towers in South America, Central America and Africa; most Central American revenue and costs are in U.S. dollars.

businessLines.name: Site development
businessLines.how: Fees per project; lumpy and low margin compared with leasing.
businessLines.description: Construction, zoning and permitting services for carriers.
